Foundational Breakthrough Investigation
Research checkpoint: 9 October 2026
1. Evidence and reproducibility
Both repositories have been pinned to immutable revisions.
Repository	Commit SHA
Astra Research Knowledge	39cdea532f19217f633f70315d92c314a6ce5e3e
OpenAI Mathematics	fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb
Astra's starting file identifies 334 scoped research cards. Its latest frontier explicitly distinguishes candidate proofs from established results and records unresolved proof obligations.
OpenAI's repository also explicitly warns that some unformalized results may contain errors. I therefore treat its manuscripts as mathematical evidence requiring reconstruction, not automatically verified theorems.
Completion criterion: A new implication must resolve an independently important foundational question. Reproducing a major result from the October release, or deriving an interesting consequence that falls short of that standard, does not qualify.
2. Foundational opportunity screening
A significant priority correction emerged from the literature search: KLS is no longer a clean unresolved target. Preprints dated 4 and 6 October 2026 independently claim dimension-free Poincaré bounds for isotropic log-concave measures. Their correctness still requires scrutiny, but a new proof cannot claim priority without resolving these overlapping claims. 


alphaXiv
+1



I identified five distinct targets:
Target	New mechanism worth testing	Main unresolved interface
Gaussian standard-simplex conjecture	Newly claimed dimension-free Gaussian propeller inequality	First Gaussian moments versus the entire noise-stability spectrum
Polynomial worst-case trace reconstruction	Multiscale moment separation and convex prefix decoding	Replace quasipolynomial separation losses with polynomial ones
Higher-dimensional Kakeya maximal conjecture	Density-sensitive tube geometry and two-frame entropy comparisons	Control higher-dimensional projection and clustering configurations
Thin bases beyond graphs	Simultaneous cut and tree-packing matrix sparsification	Transfer graphic-cut structure to genuinely non-graphic matroids
KLS and stronger convex-measure inequalities	Gaussian prediction and high-order tensor methods	Establish novelty relative to the October KLS proof claims
